conventions.convention: The Hodge page uses coordinate roots α_i=x_i−x_{i+1}, coordinate coroots and adjacent Cartan entries −1. The published diagrammatic balanced roots differ by alternating signs and are not used for trace positivity or descent signs.
S=ℝ[x_1,…,x_n], deg x_i=2, and M(d)_e=M_{d+e}; the external shift (d) equals the library internal shift {−d}. Strict dominance means c_1>⋯>c_n for ρ=Σc_jx_j.

Reduction is by the right augmentation: overline M=M/MS_+. The Lefschetz operator is left multiplication by ρ. The notation dim overline M is defined as the Laurent polynomial Σ dimℝ(overline M^i)v^(−i).
The Hecke pairing is A-bilinear, not sesquilinear: (h,h′)=ε(a(h)h′), with a(v)=v and a(H_x)=H_{x⁻¹}. The normalized standard basis is orthonormal.

The Bott-Samelson trace extracts the coefficient of the all-c_s tensor in the right basis. Invariant forms are symmetric, right-S-bilinear and left-invariant; they need not be left-S-bilinear. Non-degeneracy here means the induced map to the right dual is an isomorphism.

Primitives are P_L^(−i)=ker L^(i+1) on H^(−i). Standard HR includes hard Lefschetz and primitive sign (−1)^((d−i)/2), where −d is the bottom degree. Opposite-parity spaces are zero. Intrinsic HR(x) includes S(x); embedded HRbar is formulated independently of S(x).

Perverse means a nonnegative integer combination of KL basis elements. For p-split objects, τ_≤j selects shifts k≥−j. In cohomological degree i, pK_≥0 requires k≤i and pK_≤0 requires k≥i. Minimality means every differential lies in the categorical radical.
L_ζ is left multiplication by ρ plus ζ times middle multiplication by ρ, with ζ≥0. Bimodule summands are automatically L_0-stable; positive-parameter stability requires an additional condition.
The local form is on degree-zero Hom: E_y=Hom⁰(B_y,B_xB_s), with (f,g)=g* f∈End⁰(B_y)=ℝ. Its dimension is distinguished from the graded rank of the full Hom module.

load_bearing.statement: Over k=ℚ or k=ℝ, the bimodule Soergel category has unique finite Krull-Schmidt decompositions. For every x∈S_n there is a unique normalized indecomposable B_x supported on {y:y≤x} with top Δ layer exactly Δ_x=R_x(−ℓ(x)). It is the unique summand with the x graph of any reduced Bott-Samelson word for x. Every indecomposable is exactly one B_x(d). Its finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism algebra is local, with residue field k under restriction to its rank-one top layer. No Kazhdan-Lusztig character identity is assumed.

Over k=ℚ or ℝ, normalized B_x is isomorphic to its right dual. Its right reduction has degrees only in [−ℓ(x),ℓ(x)], all congruent to ℓ(x) modulo two, and the two extremal dimensions are one. Every Bott-Samelson word has a graded perfect symmetric invariant trace form. These assertions assume neither the character conjecture nor hard Lefschetz.

Real extension preserves normalized indecomposable labels, shifts, support-filtration multiplicities, characters, reductions and Hom spaces. If xs>x and S(y) holds for all y<xs, then B_xB_s=B_xs⊕⊕_{y<xs}B_y^{a_y}, with nonnegative integer multiplicities and no shifts, and the top summand occurs once. If xs<x and S(x) holds, then B_xB_s=B_x(1)⊕B_x(−1).

For a reduced expression of x, every upper Bruhat support layer of its positive Rouquier complex, or its minimal subcomplex, is homotopy equivalent to Δ_x when the layer label is x and to zero otherwise. No positivity of characters and no assumption S is used.

Assume S(y) for all y≤x. A minimal positive Rouquier complex has degree-zero term B_x and, for every i≥1, degree-i term ⊕_{z<x}B_z(i)^{m_{z,i}}. It is linear, with m_{z,i}=0 unless i≡ℓ(x)−ℓ(z) modulo two; its Euler multiplicities give the signed nonnegative inverse KL coefficients.

For ζ>0 and xs<x, S(x) and hL(x) imply hL(x,s)_ζ. For ζ>0 and xs>x, S(≤x), all lower ascent HR statements, HRbar(<x,s)_ζ and HR(x) imply hL(x,s)_ζ. For ζ=0 and xs>x, S(≤x), all lower ascent HR statements, HR(x) and hL(z) for every z<xs imply hL(x,s). Centered hard Lefschetz fails for ζ=0 and xs<x.

For xs>x, assume S(y) and HR(y) for every y<xs. Bottom evaluation injects Hom⁰(B_y,B_xB_s) into the primitive space in degree −ℓ(y), and identifies its local form with the primitive Lefschetz form up to the positive bottom normalization factor. Consequently HR(x,s) implies S(xs).

A Soergel bimodule satisfying hL and standard HR has induced hL and standard HR on B B_s for ζ sufficiently large. If hL(x,s)_ζ holds for every ζ≥0, HR at one parameter propagates to every nonnegative parameter; HR(x) supplies a sufficiently large starting parameter.

For every w∈S_n, Soergel's conjecture S(w), hard Lefschetz hL(w) and the Hodge-Riemann relations HR(w) hold; and for every x,s with xs>x the strong forms HRbar(x,s)_ζ hold for all ζ≥0. The proof starts with the unit and maintains all ascent and positive-descent parameter statements in finite length order.

concerns.concern: F7 and step 4.2 assert F_xF_s∈pK^b_≥0 under S(≤x), but the cited linearity theorem explicitly proves bounds for F_x under S(≤x), not tensor preservation for an arbitrary additional s. Its ascent argument, step 4.1, uses S(zs), which cannot simply be imported here before S(xs). A short noncircular justification is available: S(z) makes the standard coefficients of KL_z nonnegative filtration multiplicities, hence μ(y,z)≥0; the simple multiplication formula then makes an ascent B_zB_s perverse without S(zs). Together with the proved descent contraction and the stupid filtration, this gives the required tensor bound. That justification should be stated before using it to obtain the forward cancellation.

The Example and step 1.1 write dim(overline B_sB_t)=1+1+1+1=4. This is correct for ordinary real dimension, but def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator explicitly reserves dim overline M for the graded Laurent polynomial. Here that polynomial is v²+2+v⁻². Specify ordinary dimension or evaluation at v=1 to distinguish the two conventions.

seams_checked.note: Checked the page and its three actual consuming items in both interface directions. They preserve right origin reduction, external shifts, top-support labels and normalized duality. The projective dictionary explicitly proves extension from ℚ to ℂ in step 5.1 using rational Hom equations and the nilpotent radical; it does not attribute complex indecomposability directly to the real-only comparison statement. Its wall-crossing and multiplicity comparisons distinguish polynomial bimodules, coinvariant bimodules and origin reductions. The Hodge suppliers do not use these category-O consumers as prerequisites.
